bash: Execute a shell command and return its output. Run one command per call; do not chain with ; or &&. Use background for long-running commands.
edit: Replace exact text in a file. oldString must match uniquely unless replaceAll is true. Preserve indentation; omit line-number prefixes. Read the file first and copy the exact text; never guess oldString.
write: Write a file, overwriting if it exists. Creates missing parent directories. Use edit for partial changes.
read: Read a file or directory. Lines are prefixed with line numbers. Use offset and limit for large files.
glob: Find files by glob pattern, e.g. "**/*.ts".
grep: Search file contents by regex or literal text. Returns file paths, line numbers, and previews.
webfetch: Fetch content from a URL as text, markdown, or HTML. Read-only.
websearch: Search the web for current information beyond the knowledge cutoff.
